channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: 38% veem Lula prejudicado pela crise no STF; 31% citam Flávio
item.description: A September 2026 Datafolha poll shows 38% of respondents believe Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) is the presidential candidate most harmed by the STF and Banco Master crisis, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) with 31%. The crisis is expected to influence voting decisions, according to 47% of respondents.

item.title: Enganação até o 1° turno: como Flávio tenta driblar as investigações
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro faces new setback after revelations about his relationship with lawyer Willer Tomaz, investigated in the INSS fraud scheme, involving a safari in South Africa, private jet flights and use of an apartment coveted by Daniel Vorcaro's nephew.

item.title: As desculpas de Cármen Lúcia
item.description: Justice Carmen Lucia apologized to Brazilian society for not helping calm tensions at the Supreme Court during a controversial session. The author criticizes the lack of ethical consensus in Brazil and points to the Supreme Court as a power without checks and balances, citing international accountability cases. The text highlights polarization around Alexandre de Moraes and the absence of concrete ethical sanctions in Brazil.

item.title: TSE suspende regra e presos provisórios poderão votar em 2026
item.description: The TSE (Superior Electoral Court) decided to suspend the voting ban for pretrial detainees established by the Anti-Fraud Law, allowing them to vote in the 2026 elections, although in smaller numbers due to bureaucratic restrictions. The decision is based on the principle of electoral annuuality, which prevents legislative changes less than one year before the election.

item.title: Lula: “Votar nas mulheres de direita não dá certo”
item.description: President Lula stated during a rally in Guarulhos that voting for right-wing women does not work, advocating support for left-wing candidates such as Marina Silva and Simone Tebet for the Senate in São Paulo. His remark sparked mixed reactions, standing out in the gender and partisan debate within the Brazilian electoral landscape of 2026.

item.title: ‘Sonso’, ‘mentiroso’ e ‘cara de pau’: Gonet é alvo de críticas após foto com Vorcaro
item.description: A photo of the Attorney General, Paulo Gonet, with banker Daniel Vorcaro in London sparked criticism from politicians who questioned the alleged lack of connection between the two. Gonet had previously denied, during a STF session, having any closeness to Vorcaro. Lawmakers like Nikolas Ferreira and Romeu Zema labeled the prosecutor as 'liar' and 'tedious', intensifying the debate on ethics and public image of authorities.

item.title: Ala do PL diz que agenda do vice de Flávio foi suspensa por falta de quórum
item.description: Alfredo Gaspar (PL), running mate of Flávio Bolsonaro, had his campaign event suspended in Irecê (BA), with organizers citing Anac's recommendation about aerodrome conditions, while a PL faction blamed low turnout and mobilization challenges. The event followed Flávio's campaign activities in Vitória da Conquista.

item.title: Rui Costa Pimenta quer ampliar direitos trabalhistas e verbas da saúde
item.description: Rui Costa Pimenta, PCO candidate for president, proposes expanding labor rights and investing in public health with more funding, hospital construction, and professional hiring. His proposals include public education nationalization, expropriation of vacant properties, land reform, and salary increases. He advocates progressive policies such as opening medical schools without entrance exams and demarcating indigenous lands.

item.title: Caiado promete governo "transformador" e reformas estruturais
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado, PSD presidential candidate, proposes a 'transformative' government focused on security, fiscal responsibility, and productive growth. He advocates for harsher penalties, a new public security ministry, and inter-branch cooperation to pass structural reforms.

item.title: A nova pesquisa Datafolha sobre a disputa Lula x Flávio no maior colégio eleitoral do Brasil
item.description: A new Datafolha poll, registered as BR-09355/2026 and conducted between September 22 and 24, 2026, examines the 2026 electoral race in São Paulo, covering presidential, state, and senatorial contests. The survey tests thirteen first-round presidential candidates, including Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro, Zema, and Ronaldo Caiado, along with five second-round scenarios, emphasizing the Lula versus Flávio matchup. The poll also includes a section on the Supreme Federal Court's performance, addressing ethics, suspicions in the Banco Master case, and the court's influence on candidate campaigns. The survey includes 1.610 interviews with a ±2-point margin of error, scheduled for release on September 24.

item.title: Abin alerta governo Lula sobre interferência "crítica" dos EUA nas eleições
item.description: The Abin warned the Lula government about risks of US electoral interference in 2026, highlighting geopolitical pressures and sanctions linked to figures like Eduardo Bolsonaro. The report indicates the Trump administration prioritizes regional control and views Brazil as an obstacle to US influence in Latin America.

item.title: Facções ou 8/1: Lula contesta Trump e liga terrorismo a Bolsonaro
item.description: On the Noblat program, Lula criticized Trump and linked Bolsonaro to state terrorism, referencing the January 8th coup plots. The parliamentary caucus discussed the risk of a Flávio Bolsonaro government with a seven-vote majority in the Supreme Court, with appointments of up to five ministers.

item.title: Lula na defensiva, Flávio no ataque: como a crise no STF já afeta as campanhas eleitorais
item.description: The STF crisis, marked by corruption suspicions involving justices and former banker Daniel Vorcaro, is directly influencing the 2026 election campaign, putting Lula on the defensive and Flávio Bolsonaro on the attack. The presidential race has lost focus on issues like economy, health, and public security, with 7% of voters undecided after PF revelations.

item.title: Renan propõe cortes na Previdência e alterar pisos da saúde e educação
item.description: Renan Santos, candidate from the Missão party, proposes pension cuts, unlinks health and education floors from RCL, and replaces Bolsa Família with Citizen Fronts. His plan includes a fiscal adjustment of R$1.1 trillion by 2031, federal oversight of inefficient municipalities, and doubled infrastructure investments.

item.title: Norte é pouco representado em pesquisas eleitorais, diz especialista
item.description: Political scientist Naiara Alcantara pointed out the underrepresentation of Northern Brazilian voters in electoral polls, noting the scarcity of research companies in the region. She analyzed the tension between economic development and environmental preservation, especially regarding oil exploration in the Equatorial Margin, and stressed that environmental concern does not necessarily translate into electoral choices. Alcantara also highlighted Lula's strength among Northern voters, attributing it to the socioeconomic profile and the presence of social public policies.

item.title: Nova Paraná Pesquisas mostra Zucco e Juliana Brizola na disputa pela liderança no RS
item.description: A new survey by Paraná Pesquisas shows federal deputy Luciano Zucco (PL) leading the race for governor of Rio Grande do Sul with 36.4% of voting intentions, followed by Juliana Brizola (PDT) with 31.3%. The Senate race indicates Manuela D'Ávila (PSOL) in the lead with 32.2% of voting intentions.

item.title: Caminhos para o STF recuperar a imagem
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court of Brazil faces a deepening institutional credibility crisis, exacerbated by postponed rulings and internal disputes among justices, particularly regarding Alexandre de Moraes. Legal scholars emphasize the need for cultural reforms within the Court, including term limits and greater transparency. The ongoing crisis affects other institutions such as the Federal Police and the Senate, which closely watch the Court's developments.

item.title: Frase do dia
item.description: Lula states that, if it depends on his personal will, he will end online betting in the country, viewing it as a vice and a disease, and that the government must prioritize protecting the lives of citizens, especially the poor, rather than focusing solely on tax collection.

item.title: O prazo de Lula para bater o martelo sobre a medida anti-bets
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva intends to issue a provisional measure to restrict online betting, particularly the so-called 'Tigrinho games', before the first round of elections on October 4. The initiative, to be discussed with ministers after returning from the UN, faces internal government division, with the economic team showing resistance. Lula supports the measure to protect young people, citing football champions who won titles without betting.

item.title: Filho de Covas declara apoio a Lula e diz que Flávio é muito pior que o pai
item.description: Mário Covas Neto, former São Paulo city councilor and son of Governor Mário Covas, endorsed Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) for the 2026 presidential race, following alignment with Vice President Geraldo Alckmin (PSB), who was also his father's running mate. In press statements, Zuzinha asserted that Senator Flávio Dino (PSB) is far worse than his father, Mário Covas, but emphasized that Lula represents a more viable alternative for Brazil.

item.title: Dono de ONG bancada pelo governo mobiliza campanha paralela de Lula com aval de Janja
item.description: The owner of an NGO that received R$5.6 million from the federal government leads a parallel campaign supporting Lula's reelection, using resources from Ministry of Culture civil servants and involving members of the Culture Points, without registering the actions and profiles used with the TSE.

item.title: Campanha de Lula estimula ‘missões’ diárias para militância reagir à alta de Flávio nas pesquisas
item.description: Lula's campaign launched a daily grassroots mobilization effort on social media to promote government achievements and attack Flávio Bolsonaro and Supreme Court Minister André Mendonça, amid a technical tie and Flávio's recent lead in polls. Daily 'missions' are sent via WhatsApp, encouraging sharing and conversations with undecided voters, particularly focused on reinforcing the Bolsa Família program.

item.title: Aliados tentam convencer Flávio a ir a NY entre o 1º e 2º turnos
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL) allies push for a New York trip between the first and second rounds of the 2026 elections to meet investors, but the senator prefers to stay in Brazil due to the short 20-day campaign window. The plan aims to strengthen his profile with international financial markets.

item.title: Apenas 4 dos mais de 2 mil locais de votação de SP deram mais votos a candidatas a deputada federal em 2022
item.description: In 2022, only 4 out of 2,048 polling stations in São Paulo gave more votes to female federal deputy candidates, according to analysis by Girl Up Brasil using TSE data. Female candidates exceeded 50% of nominal votes in only a few locations, while male candidates led the majority of sections. Higher-income areas such as Pinheiros and Alto de Pinheiros showed stronger support for women, whereas lower-income areas like Parelheiros and Grajaú recorded smaller proportions of votes for female candidates.

item.title: ONU propõe a candidatos medidas contra desigualdades de gênero
item.description: UN Women launched 10 proposals for Brazilian candidates to combat gender inequalities, addressing politics, violence, and economy. The initiatives aim to ensure female representation and eliminate disparities such as the 21% wage gap and 1,571 femicides in 2025.

item.title: Luta contra o rebaixamento é destaque no sábado (19/9) de Brasileirão
item.description: The 28th round of the 2026 Brasileirão, played on Saturday (September 19), highlights the relegation battle, with seven of the ten teams in relegation zone positions. Key matches include Atlético-MG vs. Chapecoense, Mirassol vs. Botafogo, and Santos vs. Remo, all with direct implications for the table. Santos and Botafogo, with the same points, compete for a spot in the Libertadores, while Chapecoense fights to avoid the relegation zone.

item.title: PREPARE O CORAÇÃO ANTES DE CLICAR! #FlávioBolsonaro, #LuladaSilva, #Eleições2026
item.description: The content features a viral post referencing potential candidates Flávio Bolsonaro and Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva for the 2026 elections, but contains no substantive information about proposals or events. It appears to be a misleading or low-value post without meaningful political analysis.

item.title: VÍDEO: posso votar no segundo turno se faltei no primeiro?
item.description: If a voter misses the first round of the 2026 elections, they can still vote in the second round, as each round is treated as a new election by the electoral court. However, the absence must be justified within 60 days, either through the e-Título app, the TSE's self-service portal, or by visiting a local electoral office with supporting documents.

item.title: Salário mínimo e aposentadoria: confira quais são as propostas dos candidatos a presidente
item.description: The 2026 presidential candidates' proposals on minimum wage and Social Security reflect divergences regarding benefit indexing. While Lula (PT) advocates maintaining real wage increases, Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) proposes digitalization and professional management without union interference, without detailing changes to indexing. The debate includes the possibility of unlinking benefits from the minimum wage, directly impacting the population's purchasing power.

item.title: Governadores pedem a Lula inclusão do gás natural no Redata
item.description: The governors of Sergipe and Amazonas asked President Lula to include natural gas as an eligible energy source for data centers under Redata, highlighting local infrastructure and risk of lost investments. The federal government has not yet defined eligible energy sources.

item.title: Lula prepara caminhada com João Campos no Recife na 6ª feira
item.description: President Lula will visit Recife on Friday to walk with João Campos, the PSB candidate for Pernambuco governor. After repeated requests, the move undermines Raquel Lyra's strategy, which sought Rui Costa's support to block the rally. An AtlasIntel poll shows a technical tie between the candidates.

item.title: Governo Lula manobrou no STF para blindar aumento do Bolsa Família, diz advogada de Flávio
item.description: The Lula government implemented a 15% increase in Bolsa Família, which was challenged by Renan Santos at the TSE. Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes ruled that the raise merely adjusts values due to inflation, protecting the government from adverse rulings. The lawyer for Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign accuses the government of an irregular maneuver combined with the Public Defender's Office.

item.title: Debate esvaziado reúne Zema, Cury e Samara em São Paulo
item.description: The presidential debate organized by Metrópoles, Inteligência Ltda., and G4 in São Paulo was hollowed out due to the absence of leading candidates, leaving only Romeu Zema, Augusto Cury, and Samara Martins. The three addressed topics such as economy, education, and criticism of the STF, with proposals ranging from privatizations to political system reforms.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro usa Comissão de Segurança como vitrine eleitoral, mas faltou a 72% das sessões
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro uses the Public Security Committee, which he chairs in the Senate, as an electoral platform, featuring it in advertisements broadcast on TV and radio. However, he missed 72% of the committee's sessions. His presence at the August session was an exception, occurring amid presidential campaign commitments.

item.title: Ministro defende que Lula divulgue carta com compromisso fiscal para novo mandato
item.description: Minister José Guimarães suggested that President Lula release a letter with fiscal commitments for a potential new term, emphasizing the need for strict economic measures in the 2026 campaign.

item.title: Samara diz que “absurdo” é o “bolsa-banqueiro”, não o Bolsa Família
item.description: Samara Martins claimed the biggest fiscal absurdity is public debt interest (R$1.8 trillion), not the Bolsa Família increase. She criticized the 6x1 work schedule and supported job creation, education, health, and renationalization of privatized companies.

item.title: Zema cita caso BRB-Master para defender privatizações de bancos
item.description: In a presidential debate, Romeu Zema (Novo) referenced the BRB and Banco Master case to criticize public institutions and advocate for the privatization of state-owned banks, linking the bank’s involvement to political interference.

item.title: Nova pesquisa mede a disputa Lula x Flávio no maior colégio eleitoral do Nordeste
item.description: A new Quaest poll (BR-03961/2026), commissioned by TV Bahia, measures the 2026 electoral race in Bahia, including presidential (Lula vs. Flávio) and gubernatorial (ACM Neto vs. Jerônimo Rodrigues) scenarios. The survey, with 900 interviews and a 3-point margin of error, assesses voting intentions, approval of Lula’s government, and electoral emotions.

item.title: Cury e Zema trocam elogios, atacam STF e confrontam Samara em debate em SP
item.description: In a debate in São Paulo, presidential candidates Romeu Zema and Augusto Cury avoided direct confrontations, exchanged compliments, and united in criticism of the STF. The two focused their attacks on Samara Martins, the only woman in the race. The debate, organized by Metrópoles and Inteligência Ltda., was considered hollow due to the lack of confrontation among candidates.

item.title: Cury diz que Lula usa “a dor dos outros” com reajuste do Bolsa Família
item.description: Augusto Cury (Avante) criticized the Bolsa Família adjustment announced by Lula near the elections, accusing the government of using the pain of recipients to gain votes. During a debate hosted by Metrópoles, Cury emphasized the importance of the increase but questioned its timing, suggesting beneficiaries deserved more than R$ 900. He also referenced a visit to Rocinha to listen to residents and criticized Lula for exploiting people's vulnerability in his campaign.

item.title: Em debate, Cury cobra Fachin por apuração do caso Master: “Doa a quem doer”
item.description: Augusto Cury urged STF president Edson Fachin to advance investigations into the Banco Master case during a debate hosted by Inteligência Ltda and Metrópoles. He proposed judicial reform with an eight-year term limit for Supreme Court justices and criticized the Senate over alleged ties to individuals connected to the case. Cury labeled the related expenditures as 'dishonest money'.

item.title: Zema no debate Metrópoles/Inteligência Ltda: “Quero o Brasil fora do Brics”
item.description: Romeu Zema proposed Brazil's withdrawal from BRICS, criticizing dependence on China and advocating greater integration with Mercosul. He noted that China accounts for over 30% of Brazil's trade and called the group a 'patchwork quilt'.

item.title: Aliada de Lula, Leila defende impeachment de Moraes em propaganda eleitoral
item.description: Senator Leila do Vôlei (PDT), an ally of Lula, publicly supported the impeachment of Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes for the first time during an electoral broadcast. She emphasized the need for investigations into alleged connections between Moraes, Daniel Vorcaro, and Banco Master.

item.title: Veja como foi a sexta-feira (18) dos candidatos a presidente
item.description: On Friday (18), presidential candidates held debates, interviews, and social events. Lula emphasized anti-addiction efforts and social policies, while others addressed entrepreneurship, labor mobilization, and community projects.

item.title: Tarcísio aponta motivação eleitoral em reajuste do Bolsa Família
item.description: The governor of São Paulo, Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos), stated that the Bolsa Família adjustment announced by President Lula (PT) has electoral motivation. He agreed with Flávio Bolsonaro's statement calling the measure an 'act of desperation' from the PT campaign.

item.title: Votar em mulheres de direita não dá certo, diz Lula
item.description: Lula stated that women should vote for left-wing candidates, citing Marina Silva and Simone Tebet as examples, during a campaign event in Guarulhos. He repudiated violence against women and emphasized the importance of women holding their heads high. The event featured Janja Lula, Geraldo Alckmin, and Fernando Haddad.

item.title: Lula diz que vai “acabar com a pouca vergonha no futebol”
item.description: President Lula reiterated at a rally in Guarulhos his intention to end 'betting markets' in football, responding to clubs opposing online betting regulations; he stated the government does not fear losing tax revenue, citing R$ 62 billion collected.

item.title: Lula x Flávio: a nova pesquisa Datafolha sobre a corrida presidencial
item.description: A new Datafolha poll commissioned by Folha de S.Paulo and Globo investigates voting intention for the 2026 presidential race with thirteen candidates, including Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro. The survey also analyzes candidate rejection rates, voting decision patterns, government evaluation, and the activity of the Supreme Court (STF). Data collection will take place from September 22 to 24 with 2,002 interviews and a two-point percentage margin of error.

item.title: Quem são e quanto ganham aliados de Paes na prefeitura do Rio
item.description: During Eduardo Paes' (PSD) term in the Rio city hall from 2021 to 2026, over 8,900 appointed positions were filled, many with political ties, costing R$ 404 million. Allies such as Dalila de Brito Ferreira (União Brasil) and Elias Jabbour (PCdoB) topped the earnings, with gross salaries exceeding the constitutional ceiling, though deductions lowered net pay.

item.title: Presidente do PT proíbe divulgação de materiais de campanha sem número de Lula
item.description: Edinho Silva, president of PT, instructed that candidates who omit Lula in campaign materials should be punished, including returning electoral funds.
